title: Joining & Leaving a Motorway
whatItIs: You usually join and leave a motorway by a slip road. Match your speed when joining, and plan your exit early.
keyFacts: On the slip road, build up your speed to match the traffic on the motorway.
Give priority to traffic already on the motorway and join where there is a safe gap.
Countdown markers show the distance to the start of the deceleration lane. Each bar is about 100 yards.
Move into the left lane well before your exit, signal left in good time, and slow down on the slip road.
After leaving, check your speedometer: you may be going faster than it feels.

visual.caption: Joining and leaving, step by step

items.title: Slip road
items.text: Build up speed to match the traffic in the left lane.

items.title: Mirrors and look
items.text: Check the motorway traffic, using mirrors and a quick sideways glance.

items.title: Join a gap
items.text: Give way to motorway traffic. Don't force your way in.

items.title: Settle in
items.text: Stay in the left lane until you are used to the speed.

items.title: Exit early
items.text: Get into the left lane early and signal left in good time.

items.title: Slow on the slip
items.text: Slow down on the slip road, not on the motorway.

a.label: Joining
points: Speed up on the slip road

b.label: Leaving
points: Slow down on the slip road

onTheTest.question: You are joining a motorway from a slip road. What should you do?
options: Give way to traffic already on the motorway
Expect motorway traffic to move over for you
Join slowly, then speed up in the left lane
Stop at the end of the slip road and wait
onTheTest.why: Traffic on the motorway has priority. Match its speed on the slip road and join where there is a safe gap.

traps: Traffic already on the motorway has priority: match its speed and fit into a safe gap.
Countdown markers count down to the start of the deceleration lane, about 100 yards per bar.
After the motorway, 50 mph can feel like 30: check your speedometer.
